model.rationale: The open seat leans Democratic by eight points, Solis holds an overwhelming money advantage with $1.4 million raised against no reported Republican receipts, and markets price the race near 97% Democratic; every available signal points the same way and nothing contradicts a wide Democratic margin.

overview:
California's 38th District is an open seat following redistricting, and its partisan lean favors Democrats by about eight points. Hilda Solis, the Democratic nominee, has raised roughly $1.4 million and drawn about $370,000 in outside support, while Republican Pedro Casas shows no reported fundraising. No public polls of the general election are available, and no expert raters have weighed in on the race.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97 percent, and the underlying fundamentals point to a Democratic margin around nineteen points. With little independent information, uncertainty is wider than usual, but district lean, the fundraising gap, and market pricing all align in the same direction. The seat is rated Safe Democratic.
